blocks.source: Physics notation ($Q$ and $Q^{GF}$ in components).
$Q$ is the free BRST–BV differential and $Q^{GF}$ the gauge-fixing operator.
On the components of the physics notation key after Section 1.2, with the slot of the image in square brackets:

The arrow $c\mapsto-\partial_mc$ of $Q$ is the linearised gauge transformation, its arrows from $A_m$, $A_{ij}$, $\lambda$ into the antifield slots are the free Maxwell, massless Klein–Gordon and Weyl operators, and in momentum space $\partial_m\mapsto ip_m$.
$Q^{GF}$ uses no antighost and no Nakanishi–Lautrup field: the Feynman-gauge condition is the arrow $A_m\mapsto\partial_mA_m$ into the ghost slot.
Physics notation (Laplacian, failed axioms, Feynman gauge).
$H=[Q,Q^{GF}]=-\partial^2$ on every component, $|p|^2$ in momentum space.
The two failed axioms in components:
(Q^{GF})^2A^*_m=-2\,\partial_mA^*_m\ [c],\qquad (Q^{GF})^2c^*=-2\,\partial_mc^*\ [A_m],\qquad Qc=-\partial_mc=Q^{GF}\big(\tfrac12\partial_mc\ [A^*_m]\big).

Remark [3.7](#b-00412): with $d^*A|_V=-\partial_mA_m$, the propagator is the covariance of $e^{S/\hbar}$ for $S$ completed by $-\tfrac14\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)$; for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, in the components of the key,
\frac S\hbar-\frac1{4\hbar}\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)\supset\int d^4x\Big\{-\tfrac14F^a_{mn}F^a_{mn}-\tfrac12(\partial_mA^a_m)^2\Big\},
the Wick image of the Feynman-gauge ($\xi=1$) term $-\tfrac12(\partial^\mu A^a_\mu)^2$, since $\partial^\mu A_\mu=\partial_mA_m$ for $A_0=iA_4$, $\partial_0=i\partial_4$.
Physics notation (heat kernel).
$K_t$ is the Schwinger proper-time (heat) kernel.

Its components are those of the BV kernel $K_0$, i.e. $-\delta(x-y)$ times the inverse of the field–antifield pairings $(A,A^*)=(A_m,A^*_m)+\tfrac14(A^{ij},A^*_{ij})$, $(\lambda,\lambda^*)=(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i)-(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i})$, $(c^*,c)$, with
\delta(x-y)\ \longrightarrow\ \frac{e^{-|x-y|^2/4t}}{(4\pi t)^2}=\int\frac{d^4p}{(2\pi)^4}\,e^{i(p,x-y)}\,e^{-t|p|^2}.

$L_t=(Q^{GF}\otimes1)K_t$ has the components of the propagator of Proposition [3.11](#b-00430) with $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}/|p|^2$ replaced by $e^{-t|p|^2}$, and $K_\infty=0$ because $e^{-t|p|^2}\to0$ for $p\neq0$.
Physics notation (regulated propagators).
$P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ is the Feynman-gauge propagator with the heat-kernel (Schwinger proper-time) regulator, $\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2}=\int_\varepsilon^\infty e^{-t|p|^2}dt$.
Each entry below is multiplied by $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}/|p|^2$, the kernel being $\int\frac{d^4p}{(2\pi)^4}e^{i(p,x-y)}(\cdots)$:
and $\langle\lambda\lambda\rangle=\langle\bar\lambda\bar\lambda\rangle=0$.
Every edge carries $\hbar P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ (Proposition 3.22).

For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $\hbar(-,-)^{-1}=\tfrac12\sum_a(-igT^a)\otimes(-igT^a)$, and in the components $A_m=-igA^a_mT^a$, $A_I=-igA^a_IT^a$, $\lambda=-\tfrac{ig}{\sqrt2}\lambda^aT^a$ of the key the edges are the canonical Euclidean propagators

\hbar\langle A^a_mA^b_n\rangle=\delta^{ab}\delta_{mn}\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2},\qquad \hbar\langle A^a_IA^b_J\rangle=\delta^{ab}\delta_{IJ}\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2},\qquad \hbar\langle\lambda^a_\alpha{}^i\,\bar\lambda^b_{\dot\beta j}\rangle=-\delta^{ab}\delta^i_j\,p_m\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\beta}\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2}.
In position space the scalar factor is the massless propagator $\frac1{4\pi^2|x-y|^2}$ times $1-e^{-|x-y|^2/4\varepsilon}$, with value $\frac1{16\pi^2\varepsilon}$ at $x=y$.
Physics notation (the two kernels at $t=\varepsilon$).
In momentum space $P(\varepsilon,\infty)\star$ is multiplication by $Q^{GF}(p)\,e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}/|p|^2$, and Proposition [3.12](#b-00445) reads, on each component,

(QQ^{GF}+Q^{GF}Q)\,\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2}=e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2},\qquad -\partial^2\,\frac{1-e^{-|x-y|^2/4\varepsilon}}{4\pi^2|x-y|^2}=\frac{e^{-|x-y|^2/4\varepsilon}}{(4\pi\varepsilon)^2},\qquad \varepsilon\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2}=-\varepsilon\,e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}:

the regulated propagator inverts the kinetic operator up to the smeared delta function $K_\varepsilon$, and the scale derivative of a graph replaces one propagator $\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2}$ by $-\varepsilon\,e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}$ with the same numerator (one Schwinger time pinned at $t=\varepsilon$, the edge $-\varepsilon L_\varepsilon$).
Physics notation (BV Laplacian, effective interaction, master equation).

• $\Delta_\varepsilon=-\partial_{K_\varepsilon}$ is the BV Laplacian regularised by the heat kernel: it contracts a field with its own antifield ($A_m$ with $A^*_m$, $A_{ij}$ with $A^*_{kl}$, $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$ with $\lambda^{*\beta}{}_j$, $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ with $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\beta j}$, $c$ with $c^*$) through $(4\pi\varepsilon)^{-2}e^{-|x-y|^2/4\varepsilon}$ in place of $\delta(x-y)$; $\{-,-\}_\varepsilon$ is the regularised antibracket, and $\{-,-\}$ of Definition [1.6](#b-00095) the BV antibracket.

• $W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),J)$ is the sum of the connected Feynman graphs with vertices from $J/\hbar$, internal lines $\hbar P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ and the background fields on the external legs: the effective interaction with all proper times $t\in[\varepsilon,\infty)$ integrated out, one-particle-reducible graphs included.
• $d_{CE}$ is the BRST differential of the constant ghosts of $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$.

Corollary 3.18: the regularised quantum master equation $(d_{CE}+Q)J+\tfrac12\{J,J\}_\varepsilon+\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon J=0$ at scale $\varepsilon$ is equivalent to $(d_{CE}+Q)\,W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),J)=0$, invariance of the effective interaction at scale $\infty$ under the free BRST differential and the global superconformal symmetry.
Physics notation (zero modes at scale $\infty$).
$P(0,\infty)\star$ is multiplication by $Q^{GF}(p)/|p|^2$, the massless Feynman-gauge propagator, and $(QQ^{GF}+Q^{GF}Q)\,|p|^{-2}=1$ for $p\neq0$.
Moment-free sections have Fourier transforms vanishing to all orders at $p=0$.
The classes on compactly supported sections sit at $p=0$:
• a constant ghost $c=X$, a global gauge rotation, with functional $-\int d^4x\,(c^*,X)$;
• harmonic polynomial scalars, $\partial^2A_{ij}=0$;
• polynomial solutions of the Weyl equations $\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i=0$, $\partial_m\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}=0$;
• in the gauge field (Remark [3.21](#b-00510)), $A_m=(a_nx_n)\,b_m$ with $a_mb_m=0$: $\partial_mA_m=0$, $\partial^2A_m=0$, and the constant field strength $F^0_{mn}=a_mb_n-a_nb_m$.
Physics notation (loop expansion and one-loop superdeterminant).

In Proposition 3.22, $b_1(\gamma)$ is the number of loops, $1/|\operatorname{Aut}\gamma|$ the symmetry factor, the Taylor components of $J$ are the vertices of the Feynman rules and $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ is the propagator.
Proposition 3.23 is the one-loop superdeterminant expanded in ring graphs with $n$ insertions and symmetry factor $\frac1{2n}$:
\big(e^{\hbar\partial_\phi}e^{J/\hbar}\big)\big|_{e=0}=\exp\Big(-\tfrac12\mathrm{STr}\log\big(1-\text{one-loop operator}\big)\Big)=\mathrm{SDet}\big(1-\text{one-loop operator}\big)^{-1/2}.

In the field theory the one-loop operator is the propagator composed with the parity operator and the second variation of the interaction at the background (the fluctuation operator), and $\mathrm{STr}$ is $\int d^4x$ times the trace over colour, Lorentz and $SU(4)$ indices, with the sign $-1$ for loops of the odd fields $\lambda$ and $c$–$A^*$.
Physics notation (unit, minimal subtraction, Schwinger integrals).

• For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and $X=-igX^aT^a$: $(X,Y)=2\hbar X^aY^a$, $\mathrm{ad}_X=-igX^aT^a_A$ with the adjoint generators $(T^a_A)^{bc}=-if^{abc}$, and $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)=-g^2N\,X^aY^a$, so that the unit $\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$ is $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$ (physics notation key after Section 1.2).

The fourth-order traces of the quartic graphs, in the unit $\frac{\hbar}{16\pi^2}$, are $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_{X_1}\mathrm{ad}_{X_2}\mathrm{ad}_{X_3}\mathrm{ad}_{X_4})=g^4X_1^aX_2^bX_3^cX_4^d\operatorname{tr}(T^a_AT^b_AT^c_AT^d_A)$.

• $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is the one-loop counterterm of the proper-time (heat-kernel) regularisation in minimal subtraction: it is purely singular, the $\varepsilon^{-1}$ (quadratically divergent) and $\log\varepsilon$ (logarithmically divergent) parts of the one-particle-irreducible graphs.
• The plane-wave value is the momentum-space amplitude with $(2\pi)^4\delta(p_1+\dots+p_k)$ stripped off; generic leg momenta are non-exceptional momenta.

• The Schwinger time $t_e$ is the proper time of the edge $e$; the centre $p_1=\frac{t_2}{t_1+t_2}p$ of Lemma [4.4](#b-00577) is the shifted loop momentum with Feynman parameter $\frac{t_2}{t_1+t_2}$, and the superficial degree, $\deg(\text{numerator})+4-2|E(\gamma)|$, is the superficial degree of divergence.
Physics notation (self-energy graphs).
The three tables are the one-loop self-energies.

Gluon: (a), (b) seagulls with a gluon, resp. scalar, loop at the quartic vertex; (c) gluon bubble; (d) scalar bubble; (e) gaugino loop; (f) ghost loop, the ghost line being the $c$–$A^*_m$ propagator.
Scalar: (a), (b) seagulls; (c) gluon–scalar bubble; (d) gaugino loop through two Yukawa vertices.
Gaugino: (a) gluon, (b) scalar exchange.
On two gluon legs, with $(-,-)$ on the colour factors,
(A(p),A(-p))=(A_m(p),A_m(-p)),\qquad (\iota_pA(p),\iota_pA(-p))=p_mp_n\,(A_m(p),A_n(-p)),
and with $\int(dA|_V,dA|_V)=\tfrac12\int(F^0_{mn},F^0_{mn})$, $\int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V)=\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)$ the plane-wave values ([4.3](#b-00644)) read

\int(A_m,A_m)\mapsto2(A_m(p),A_m(-p)),\qquad \tfrac12\int(F^0_{mn},F^0_{mn})\mapsto2\big(|p|^2\delta_{mn}-p_mp_n\big)(A_m(p),A_n(-p)),\qquad \int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)\mapsto2\,p_mp_n(A_m(p),A_n(-p)):
the $\log\varepsilon$ entries along $\int(dA|_V,dA|_V)$ are transverse, those along $\int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V)$ longitudinal.
Physics notation (the quadratic counterterm).
In components, with $\mathrm{unit}=\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$ and $F^0_{mn}=\partial_mA_n-\partial_nA_m$,
with coefficient $0$ for $\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)$, and $\tfrac14(A^{ij},A_{ij})=\sum_I(A_I,A_I)$.
For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, in the components of the key, the $\varepsilon^{-1}$ part of $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]/\hbar$ is the common mass term of the four gluon and the six scalar components,
-\frac{9g^2N}{64\pi^2\,\varepsilon}\int d^4x\,\big(A^a_mA^a_m+A^a_IA^a_I\big).
Physics notation (the logarithmic quadratic counterterm).
For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, in the components of the key, the $\log\varepsilon$ part of $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]/\hbar$ without antifields is

-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}\,\log\varepsilon\int d^4x\Big\{4\Big(-\tfrac14F^{0a}_{mn}F^{0a}_{mn}-\tfrac12\partial_mA^a_I\partial_mA^a_I\Big)+8\Big(i\,\bar\lambda^a_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_m\lambda^a_\alpha{}^i\Big)\Big\},
$4$ times the free boson Lagrangian and $8$ times the free gaugino Lagrangian, and the ghost term is $-\mathrm{unit}\,\log\varepsilon\int(\partial_mc,A^*_m)$ (Remark 4.17).

The gluon part is transverse, $2(|p|^2\delta_{mn}-p_mp_n)$ in plane waves, the $p_mp_n$ coefficients $-\tfrac18$ of the gluon bubble and $+\tfrac18$ of the ghost loop cancelling; the gluon and scalar entries combine into a functional of the ten-component field $A_M=(A_m,A_I)$.
Physics notation (power counting).

The Weyl weights are mass dimensions: $[A_m]=[A_I]=1$, $[\lambda_\alpha{}^i]=[\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}]=\tfrac32$, $[c]=0$, $[A^*]=3$, $[\lambda^*]=\tfrac52$, $[c^*]=4$, $[\partial_m]=1$; the superficial degree of divergence of a one-loop graph is $4$ minus the dimensions of its legs.
Quadratic divergences ($\varepsilon^{-1}$) sit in the mass terms $\int(A_m,A_m)$ and $\int(A_I,A_I)$ alone, and $\log\varepsilon$ multiplies local functionals of dimension $4$.

The leg sets of the proposition are: the self-energies of $A_m$, $A_I$, $\lambda$ and the ghost–antifield pair $(c,A^*_m)$; the three-gluon vertex, the gluon–scalar–scalar vertex $A_mA_IA_I$, the gluon–gaugino vertex $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}A_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i$, the Yukawa vertices $\lambda^jA_{ji}\lambda^i$ and $\bar\lambda_jA^{ji}\bar\lambda_i$, the antifield (BRST-source) vertices $cA_mA^*_m$, $cA^{ij}A^*_{ij}$, $c\lambda\lambda^*$, $c\,c\,c^*$; and the four-point functions $(A_m)^4$, $(A_m)^2(A_I)^2$, $(A_I)^4$.
Physics notation (cubic tree vertices).
The tree vertices of the cubic tables are the cubic terms of $S$ in components:
• three-gluon: $-\tfrac18(F_{mn},F_{mn})\supset-\tfrac14(F^0_{mn},[A_m,A_n])$;
• gluon–scalar–scalar: $-\tfrac1{16}(D_mA^{ij},D_mA_{ij})\supset-\tfrac18(\partial_mA^{ij},[A_m,A_{ij}])=-\tfrac12\sum_I(\partial_mA_I,[A_m,A_I])$;

• gluon–gaugino: $i(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}[A_m,\lambda_\alpha{}^i])$, from $i(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}D_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i)$, pairing $S_+\otimes W$ with $S_-\otimes W^*$;
• Yukawa: $-\tfrac12(\lambda^j[A_{ji},\lambda^i])-\tfrac12(\bar\lambda_j[A^{ji},\bar\lambda_i])$, the two structures of equal chirality;

• antifield vertices: $([A_m,c],A^*_m)$, $\tfrac14([A^{ij},c],A^*_{ij})$, $([c,\lambda_\alpha{}^i],\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i)-([c,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}],\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i})$, $\tfrac12([c,c],c^*)$.

In this order the one-loop $\log\varepsilon$ coefficients are $\mathrm{unit}\cdot\log\varepsilon$ times $6$, $6$, $10$, $10$ and $1$, $1$, $1$, $1$ times the tree vertex; for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $\mathrm{unit}=-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$ and $[X,Y]^c=g\,f^{abc}X^aY^b$ in the components $X=-igX^aT^a$.
Physics notation (quartic colour and Lorentz factors).
The quartic tree vertex is the quartic part of the bosonic action,
-\tfrac18([A_m,A_n],[A_m,A_n])-\tfrac14\sum_I([A_m,A_I],[A_m,A_I])-\tfrac18\sum_{I,J}([A_I,A_J],[A_I,A_J]),
the last two terms being $-\tfrac1{16}([A_m,A^{ij}],[A_m,A_{ij}])$ and $-\tfrac1{128}([A^{ij},A^{kl}],[A_{ij},A_{kl}])$.
For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ the colour factors are

([X_1,X_2],[X_3,X_4])=2\hbar g^2f^{abe}f^{cde}X_1^aX_2^bX_3^cX_4^d,\qquad \tfrac1{24}\sum_{\mathrm{orderings}}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_{X_1}\mathrm{ad}_{X_2}\mathrm{ad}_{X_3}\mathrm{ad}_{X_4})=g^4X_1^aX_2^bX_3^cX_4^d\;\tfrac1{24}\sum_{\mathrm{orderings}}\operatorname{tr}(T^a_AT^b_AT^c_AT^d_A),
the second being the totally symmetrised adjoint trace; the Lorentz factors are $(v_1,v_2)=v_{1m}v_{2m}$ on gluon legs and $(v_1,v_2)=v_{1I}v_{2I}=\tfrac14v_1^{ij}v_{2ij}$ on scalar legs.
In each quartic set the symmetrised adjoint trace cancels and the total is $8\cdot\mathrm{unit}\cdot\log\varepsilon$ times the tree vertex.
Physics notation (field rescaling).
In components the field-counting functional is
2\!\int\!\Big[(A_m,A^*_m)+\tfrac14(A^{ij},A^*_{ij})\Big]-4\!\int\!\Big[(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i)-(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i})\Big]-\!\int\!(c^*,c),
whose antibracket counts fields (Lemma 4.21).

To first order in the unit, $S$ minus the $\log\varepsilon$ part of $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is $S$, with its terms in $F_{mn}$, $D_mA_{ij}$, $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}D_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i$, the Yukawa and the ghost terms, evaluated on the rescaled fields
a one-loop wave-function renormalisation.

For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, at fixed $g$: $A^a_m,A^a_I\mapsto\big(1+\frac{g^2N}{16\pi^2}\log\varepsilon\big)A^a_m,A^a_I$, $\lambda^a\mapsto\big(1+\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}\log\varepsilon\big)\lambda^a$, $c\mapsto\big(1+\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}\log\varepsilon\big)c$.
Physics notation (coupling and mass term).

Corollary 4.23: $g$ enters through $(X,Y)=-\frac{4\hbar}{g^2}\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ alone, as the overall factor $\frac1{g^2}$ of $S$ in the fields $A_m$, $A_{ij}$, $\lambda$, so a renormalisation of $g$ is a multiple of $S$ in the $\log\varepsilon$ counterterm; that multiple is $0$.
In the usual notation $Z_g=1$ at one loop, and the counterterm is the wave-function renormalisation of Theorem 4.22.
Remark 4.24 in components:
\big(Q+\{I,-\}\big)\Big(\tfrac94\,\mathrm{unit}\,\varepsilon^{-1}\!\int\!\Big[(A_m,A_m)+\tfrac14(A^{ij},A_{ij})\Big]\Big)=-\tfrac92\,\mathrm{unit}\,\varepsilon^{-1}\!\int(\partial_mc,A_m),

from the arrow $c\mapsto-\partial_mc$ of $Q$ in the gluon mass term: the breaking of the Slavnov–Taylor identity by the regulator, $+\frac{9g^2N}{64\pi^2\varepsilon}\int(\partial_mc,A_m)$ for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$.
Physics notation (the obstruction).
With $d^*(A|_V)=-\partial_mA_m$ and $d^*dc=-\partial^2c$, the functionals of Lemma [4.28](#b-00846) are $\int(\partial_mc,A_m)$ and $\int(\partial^2c,\partial_mA_m)$, and the limit of the theorem is

-\tfrac{27}8\,\mathrm{unit}\int(\partial^2c,\partial_mA_m)=\tfrac{27}{16}\,\mathrm{unit}\;Q\!\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n),\qquad Q\!\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)=-2\!\int(\partial^2c,\partial_mA_m),
the $\varepsilon^{-1}$ terms $-\tfrac92$ (bubbles with one special edge) and $+\tfrac92$ (vertex $-QI^{CT}[\varepsilon]$) times $\mathrm{unit}\,\varepsilon^{-1}\int(\partial_mc,A_m)$ cancelling.
This is the violation of the Slavnov–Taylor identity of the gluon two-point function: by Remark 4.31 it is $Q$ of the local longitudinal ($p_mp_n$) part of the renormalised gluon self-energy,
\tfrac{27}{16}\,\mathrm{unit}\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)=-\frac{27g^2N}{256\pi^2}\,\hbar\int d^4x\,(\partial_mA^a_m)^2\quad\text{for }\mathfrak{su}(N).
Physics notation (the finite counterterm).
I\ \mapsto\ I-\tfrac{27}{16}\,\mathrm{unit}\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n),\qquad \mathfrak{su}(N):\quad \frac I\hbar\ \mapsto\ \frac I\hbar+\frac{27g^2N}{256\pi^2}\int d^4x\,(\partial_mA^a_m)^2,
a finite multiple of the Feynman-gauge term $-\tfrac12(\partial_mA^a_m)^2$ of Remark 3.7.
It cancels the local longitudinal part of the gluon self-energy, and with it the $(c,A_m)$ part of the Slavnov–Taylor violation.
It is fixed up to multiples of $\int(dA|_V,dA|_V)=\tfrac12\int(F^0_{mn},F^0_{mn})$, i.e. of $\int d^4x\,F^{0a}_{mn}F^{0a}_{mn}$, which is $Q$-closed: a renormalisation condition.
Physics notation (defect vertex, special edge, special conformal variation).

• The defect vertex $QJ+\tfrac12\{J,J\}_\varepsilon+\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon J$ measures the failure of the regularised quantum master equation (Zinn-Justin equation) at scale $\varepsilon$; its flow, $Q\,W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),J)$, measures the failure of the Slavnov–Taylor identities of the effective interaction at scale $\infty$.

• The special edge $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ is the smeared minus the sharp field–antifield contraction: in momentum space $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$ times the components of $K_0$, a Schwinger time in $[0,\varepsilon]$.
Loops closing at one cubic vertex carry $f^{abc}\delta^{bc}=0$.
• Proposition [4.35](#b-00878) in components, for $v^m=x^2v_1^m-2(v_1\cdot x)x^m$ and $(L_vA)_m=v^n\partial_nA_m+A_n\partial_mv^n$:
2\int(\partial_mA_m,\partial_n(L_vA)_n)=8\int(\partial_mA_m,v_{1n}A_n)\neq0:
the Feynman-gauge term is invariant under translations, rotations and the dilatation and breaks the special conformal transformations.
• Remark [4.34](#b-00876): the cubic sectors of the obstruction are $(c,A_m,A_n)$, $(c,A_I,A_J)$, $(c,\lambda,\lambda)$ and $(c,c,A^*_m)$.
Physics notation (sources and renormalised insertions).

• $\omega=\omega_{1234}(x)\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4$ is a compactly supported source and $O=\int d^4x\,\omega_{1234}(x)\,(\text{density})$ couples it to a composite operator; $\delta$ keeps the first order in the source, and the Weyl weight $w_O$ is the mass dimension of the composite operator.

• $O(\varepsilon)=O-\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is the bare composite operator with its one-loop operator counterterms: operator renormalisation and mixing, including mixing with the identity $\int\omega$.

• $O[\infty]$ is the renormalised insertion: the $\varepsilon\to0$ limit of the connected graphs with one vertex $O(\varepsilon)$, vertices from $I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$, lines $\hbar P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ and the background fields on the legs.
• $(d_{CE}+Q)\,O[\infty]$ is the action on the insertion of the free BRST differential and of the constant superconformal ghosts.
Physics notation (operator counterterms and BRST invariance).

Proposition 5.3: the graphs with the insertion off the loop are renormalised by the action counterterm $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$, and the operator counterterm is the $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $\log\varepsilon$ part of the graphs with the insertion on the loop, whose superficial degree of divergence is $w_O$ minus the mass dimensions of the legs.
The cocycle condition $Q\,O[\infty]=0$ is BRST invariance of the renormalised insertion.
An output of the type $\int\omega\,(\partial_mc,A_m)$ is removed by a finite multiple of the gluon mass operator $\int\omega\,(A_m,A_m)$, since
Q\int\omega\,(A_m,A_m)=-2\int\omega\,(\partial_mc,A_m),
from the arrow $c\mapsto-\partial_mc$ of $Q$.
Physics notation (colour contractions, vertices, logarithms).
For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $\hbar(-,-)^{-1}=\tfrac12\sum_a(-igT^a)\otimes(-igT^a)$, and with $X=-igX^aT^a$ Lemma [5.7](#b-00935) reads

[-,-]\ \text{on}\ (-,-)^{-1}:\ f^{abc}\delta^{ab}=0,\qquad (-,-)\ \text{on}\ (-,-)^{-1}=N^2-1,\qquad ([X_1,-],[X_2,-])\ \text{on}\ (-,-)^{-1}=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_{X_1}\mathrm{ad}_{X_2})=g^2N\,X_1^aX_2^a .
The cubic vertex of Lemma 5.8 is the gluon–scalar–scalar vertex of $-\tfrac1{16}(D_mA^{ij},D_mA_{ij})=-\tfrac14\sum_I(D_mA_I,D_mA_I)$, and the quartic one the quartic part of the bosonic action.

Lemma 5.10: the $\log\varepsilon$ coefficient of a logarithmically divergent one-loop graph is $-\frac1{16\pi^2}$ times the angular average of the top-degree part of its numerator; for the basic bubble

\int\frac{d^4p}{(2\pi)^4}\,\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}}{|p|^2}\,\frac{e^{-\varepsilon|p+p_1|^2}}{|p+p_1|^2}\ \supset\ -\frac{\log\varepsilon}{16\pi^2},\qquad \Big(\frac{1-e^{-|x-y|^2/4\varepsilon}}{4\pi^2|x-y|^2}\Big)^2\ \supset\ -\frac{\log\varepsilon}{16\pi^2}\,\delta(x-y).
Physics notation (single letters).
In components, for $X\in\mathfrak g$, $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, $v\in V$ and $\zeta=(\zeta^\alpha{}_i,\bar\zeta^{\dot\alpha i})\in\Sigma^*\otimes\mathfrak g$:
\int\omega\,(X,\iota_wA)=\int\omega\,w_I(X,A_I)=\tfrac14\int\omega\,w^{ij}(X,A_{ij}),\qquad \int\omega\,(X,\iota_v(A|_V))=\int\omega\,v_m(X,A_m),
\int\omega\,(\zeta,\lambda)=\int\omega\,\big[(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\zeta^\alpha{}_i)-(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\zeta^{\dot\alpha i})\big],\qquad \int\omega\,(X,c).
For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $(X,A_I)=2\hbar X^aA^a_I$ and $(X,A_m)=2\hbar X^aA^a_m$.

The letters are the elementary fields: the scalars $A^a_I$ in the $\mathbf 6$ of $SO(6)$ (as $A_{ij}$, the antisymmetric $\mathbf 6$ of $SU(4)$), the gluon $A^a_m$, the gaugini $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$ in $(\mathbf 2,\mathbf 1,\mathbf 4)$ and $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ in $(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 2,\bar{\mathbf 4})$ with sources $\zeta^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar\zeta^{\dot\alpha i}$, and the ghost $c$.

Proposition 5.11: a letter lies off every loop, the tadpoles carry $f^{abc}\delta^{bc}=0$, the other loops are renormalised by $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$, and the operator counterterm vanishes, $O(\varepsilon)=O$.
Physics notation ($\mathbf{20'}$ and Konishi).
With $\phi_I=A^a_IT^a$, i.e. $A_I=-ig\,\phi_I$, one has $(A_I,A_J)=4\hbar\operatorname{tr}(\phi_I\phi_J)=2\hbar\,\phi^a_I\phi^a_J$ and
\int\omega\,(\iota_{w_1}A,\iota_{w_2}A)=w_{1I}w_{2J}\int\omega\,(A_I,A_J)=\tfrac1{16}\,w_1^{ij}w_2^{kl}\int\omega\,(A_{ij},A_{kl})=4\hbar\,w_{1I}w_{2J}\int\omega\operatorname{tr}(\phi_I\phi_J).
Under $\mathrm{Spin}(6)\cong SU(4)$, $\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathbf 6=\mathbf{20'}\oplus\mathbf 1$.
The bracket of (5.6) is the $\mathbf{20'}$ ($[0,2,0]$ of $SU(4)$); in $SO(6)$ and in $SU(4)$ form, with $\phi_{ij}=\phi_I\Sigma^I_{ij}$ and $\phi^{ij}=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{ijkl}\phi_{kl}$,

4\hbar\,w_{1I}w_{2J}\int\omega\operatorname{tr}\big(\phi_I\phi_J-\tfrac16\delta_{IJ}\phi_K\phi_K\big)=\tfrac\hbar4\,w_1^{ij}w_2^{kl}\int\omega\Big[\operatorname{tr}(\phi_{ij}\phi_{kl})-\tfrac1{12}\varepsilon_{ijkl}\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{mn}\phi_{mn})\Big].
The trace part is $\tfrac16(w_1,w_2)$, $(w_1,w_2)=w_{1I}w_{2I}$, times the Konishi operator

\int\omega\,(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})=\tfrac14\int\omega\,(A^{ij},A_{ij})=4\hbar\int\omega\operatorname{tr}(\phi_I\phi_I)=\hbar\int\omega\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{ij}\phi_{ij}).
Physics notation (the insertion graphs).

In physics terms: (a) the self-contraction $\langle\phi^a_I\phi^b_J\rangle$ of the two scalars of the operator at coincident points; (b) one external gluon through a gluon–scalar–scalar vertex, with colour factor $f^{abc}\delta^{bc}=0$; (c) the seagull bubble through $-\tfrac14\sum_I([A_m,A_I],[A_m,A_I])$ and (d) the triangle through two gluon–scalar–scalar vertices, both with external gluons; (e) the bubble through the scalar potential $-\tfrac18\sum_{I,J}([A_I,A_J],[A_I,A_J])$ and (f) the triangle with a gluon exchanged between the two scalar lines, both with external scalars.
With $w_O=2$, power counting leaves at most two external bosons.
Physics notation (renormalised $\mathbf{20'}$ and Konishi operators).
In components,

\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]=\mathrm{unit}\,\log\varepsilon\Big[\tfrac14\int\omega\,(w_1^{ij}A_{ij},w_2^{kl}A_{kl})-\tfrac18\,w_1^{ij}w_{2ij}\int\omega\,(A^{kl},A_{kl})\Big]+\frac{\hbar\dim\mathfrak g\;w_1^{ij}w_{2ij}}{32\pi^2\,\varepsilon}\int\omega,
$\mathrm{unit}=\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$.
For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ ($\mathrm{unit}=-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$, $\dim\mathfrak g=N^2-1$) every $\mathbf{20'}$ operator $O$ is multiplicatively renormalised,
O(\varepsilon)=\Big(1+\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}\log\varepsilon\Big)O,
and the Konishi operator $\int\omega\,(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})=2\hbar\int\omega\,\phi^a_I\phi^a_I$ mixes with the identity alone,
\int\omega\,\phi^a_I\phi^a_I\ \longmapsto\ \Big(1-\frac{g^2N}{4\pi^2}\log\varepsilon\Big)\int\omega\,\phi^a_I\phi^a_I-\frac{3(N^2-1)}{8\pi^2\,\varepsilon}\int\omega,
the last term subtracting the coincident-point value $\langle\phi^a_I\phi^a_I\rangle=\frac{6(N^2-1)}{16\pi^2\varepsilon}$ of graph (a).
